claim: A door that opens by hand gets no lever beside it; a lever opens something that cannot be opened by hand. The campaign's lever is tile 1070: 283 sprites over the 43 maps, 184 of them wall-aligned, the pushed ones mounted at a median 0.79 player heights; 280 carry a tx, the modal command is 1 (kCmdOn, 147), and 160 set trigger_push and 241 trigger_on.
evidence: the owner, 2026-11-25: 'some of the shops have lever next to it, but it just opens door the same way you would interact with them' (projects/blood-city/level/l3_theatre.py)
recount 2026-11-26 over the 43 campaign maps (every sprite of tile 1070); the 0.79 height from knowledge/blood/design/switches-v1.json by_how.pushed
projects/blood-city/level/doorswitch.py's docstring carries the same 283/280/147 (an earlier 356/351/230/316 did not reproduce and was corrected)
use: Place levers through bloodmap.switches.pressed_switch, which sets trigger_push and trigger_on; a hand-rolled one could not be pushed. Say on and off when it is to work both ways.
